title: Repeated Fatal macOS Application Crash Reports
exclusions: Counts distinct normalized fatal Apple `.ips` crash reports per Mac and process in a closed 15-minute window and reports three or more. Apple documents `.ips` JSON for macOS 12+; legacy `.crash`, hang/spindump, jetsam/resource reports marked nonfatal, and user force-quit without a fatal crash report are excluded unless separately normalized and tested. The threshold, local parser, index, source type, and exception lookup are deployment choices. A crash report does not prove malware, root cause, data loss, or user impact, and absence of reports does not prove healthy collection.
evidence: Retain the `macos_repeated_fatal_application_crashes` search, five-minute schedule, result/alert; signed parser and schema fixtures; original protected `.ips` report or approved hash/object reference; normalized event with report ID, process, bundle, OS/build, exception and fatality; monitor/parser freshness; exception revision; case/dashboard; symbolication or developer disposition; and recovery window. Crash reports may contain sensitive paths/process/user context. This documentation-only review read no endpoint report and executed no search.

controlTest.positiveScenario: At 2026-07-29T12:15:00Z ingest three normalized fatal reports for `mac-crash-01`, `ExampleApp`, with distinct `report_id` values at 12:01, 12:06, and 12:11, exception types `EXC_BAD_ACCESS`, OS build `25G86`. Expect exactly one row with `crash_count=3`, three report IDs, and first/last times.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Require zero rows for two distinct reports; duplicate ingestion of one report ID; three reports split across different processes or hosts; `fatal=false`; missing process/report ID; events outside the closed range; or an exact host/process future exception with reason, ticket, and owner. Exception expiry equal to dispatch does not suppress. Missing collector data belongs to source health.

dataSources: Apple crash reports with `.ips` extension, which Apple documents as JSON beginning with macOS 12, collected from approved system/user DiagnosticReports locations by a signed parser or file-monitor pipeline. Normalize one event per report with `_time` from report timestamp, `host`, `report_id` (stable file/report identity), `proc_name`, `bundle_id`, `proc_path` if privacy-approved, `os_version`, `os_build`, `exception_type`, `exception_signal`, `exception_message`, `termination_reason`, `fatal`, `report_path_hash`, and `parser_version`. `index=macos_diagnostics` and `sourcetype=local:apple:crash_report` are local conventions. Collection scope and PPPC/Full Disk Access must be explicitly approved.
app: Apple DiagnosticReports/Console and Xcode crash-report schema are authoritative. A deployment-owned signed `.ips` parser, Splunk Universal Forwarder file/script input, and search app provide privacy filtering, normalization, fixtures, exceptions, search, dashboard, and runbook. No Splunkbase add-on is asserted.
spl:
index=macos_diagnostics sourcetype=local:apple:crash_report earliest=-15m@m latest=@m
| eval host=lower(trim(host)), proc_name=trim(proc_name), report_id=trim(report_id), fatal=if(fatal=true() OR lower(trim(fatal))="true",1,0)
| where fatal=1 AND len(host)>0 AND len(proc_name)>0 AND len(report_id)>0
| dedup host report_id
| stats dc(report_id) AS crash_count values(report_id) AS report_ids values(bundle_id) AS bundle_ids values(exception_type) AS exception_types values(exception_signal) AS exception_signals values(os_build) AS os_builds values(parser_version) AS parser_versions min(_time) AS first_crash_time max(_time) AS last_crash_time by host proc_name
| where crash_count>=3
| lookup macos_crash_exceptions.csv host proc_name OUTPUT exception_until_epoch exception_reason ticket exception_owner
| eval exception_until_epoch=tonumber(exception_until_epoch), exception_active=if(exception_until_epoch>now() AND len(exception_reason)>0 AND len(ticket)>0 AND len(exception_owner)>0,1,0)
| where exception_active=0
| eval threshold_crashes=3, search_window_minutes=15, use_case_id="UC-1.3.5"
| table host proc_name crash_count report_ids bundle_ids exception_types exception_signals os_builds parser_versions first_crash_time last_crash_time threshold_crashes search_window_minutes use_case_id
| sort 0 -crash_count host proc_name
description: Runs every five minutes over the preceding closed 15 minutes and emits one row per lowercased Mac hostname and exact process name when at least three distinct normalized fatal `.ips` reports occur. It deduplicates report identity and preserves exception, bundle, OS build, parser, and first/last crash evidence.
value: Repeated fatal crashes identify an unstable application/host combination worth triage while avoiding a page for every isolated termination. Stable report identity and Apple exception fields give support and developers reproducible evidence for release rollback, symbolication, compatibility, or hardware investigation.
implementation: Approve system and per-user report scope, privacy retention, and PPPC access; deploy a signed parser tested against Apple's `.ips` JSON; emit one redacted normalized event per report and monitor parser/file coverage. Run the 15-minute search every five minutes, deduplicate report IDs, require three fatal reports, and alert by host/process. Correlate application version, OS build, exception, deployment, resource state, and user impact; send protected reports to authorized developers for symbolication.
visualization: Show collection/parser freshness, path coverage, parse failures, duplicate IDs, and report volume first. Then rank fatal crashes by process/version/OS build/host, display exception types and recurrence, and trend deployment cohorts. Drill down to protected report reference, symbols/build, recent update, resource state, exception, incident, and recovery. Do not expose full user paths or raw reports broadly.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable; no CIM dataset is asserted for Apple `.ips` report identity and exception structure.

knownFalsePositives:
A repeated-crash row is real, but it may be expected during controlled work.

1. **Approved application test or fault injection** — QA may intentionally trigger a crash. Verify lab/device/process/build, test ID, owner, start/end, and expected report IDs; use only an exact finite exception.

2. **Known bad rollout already being rolled back** — Many crashes during a controlled rollback remain operational evidence. Correlate package/version/ring/change and suppress notifications only for the bounded response window, not ingestion.

3. **Duplicate collection or parser identity defect** — Re-read files, path changes, CRC configuration, or unstable report IDs can inflate counts. Check source/hash/report ID, fishbucket/input changes, parser version, and `dedup`; repair collection and retain provenance.

4. **Nonfatal EXC_RESOURCE misclassified** — Apple notes some resource reports have `NON-FATAL CONDITION`. Compare raw exception note/termination semantics and parser fixture; correct `fatal` rather than suppressing the process.

**Suppression mechanism:** the SPL uses `lookup macos_crash_exceptions.csv` on exact `host,proc_name` and requires future expiry, reason, ticket, and owner. Expired, wildcard, fleet-wide, parser-outage, or missing-source exceptions do not suppress.

detailedImplementation:
## Collection and privacy

Assign macOS, privacy/legal, application development, endpoint, Splunk, and incident owners. Qualify `.ips` schema by supported macOS release; this review ran none. Apple says modern crash reports use `.ips` JSON and documents `procName` and exception dictionary fields. Build a signed parser with versioned golden reports; do not use the old `rex Process:` against modern JSON or assume every EXC_RESOURCE report terminated a process.

Approve system and user DiagnosticReports locations, retention, redaction, and access. Deploy the Universal Forwarder monitor or a bounded parser input through a managed app. If protected paths require PPPC/System Policy All Files, grant only the signed binary/code requirement after privacy review. Emit one event per complete file after close, with stable report ID/hash, report timestamp, process/bundle, OS/build, exception type/signal/message, termination data, explicit fatal classification, source reference, and parser version. Avoid raw stack, username, path, arguments, and document content in broad indexes.

Monitor expected-host/path freshness, parser errors, unsupported schema, partial files, event/index delay, duplicate report IDs, source rename/CRC behavior, forwarder permission denial, package hash/version, and retained-object access. Test `crcSalt=<SOURCE>` only with full understanding of duplicate risk; DiagnosticReports filenames are normally unique, but moving/renaming into another monitored path can reread data.

## Search and validation

Save `macos_repeated_fatal_application_crashes`, run every five minutes over a closed 15 minutes, and trigger by host/process. `dedup host report_id` prevents retries from inflating count; `dc` requires three distinct reports. Keep process identity case behavior documented; if bundle ID is stable, add a separately tested grouping strategy rather than silently merging executables.

Run fixed controls plus 2/3 reports, duplicate IDs, process case, multiple hosts/processes, fatal true/false, NON-FATAL EXC_RESOURCE, missing field, late event, legacy `.crash`, malformed/partial `.ips`, file rename, parser upgrade, exception expiry, application update/rollback, and symbol availability. Generate crashes only in an isolated test application with owner approval. Keep draft until owners accept privacy, parser/version coverage, threshold, alert delivery, and response.

## Triage and recovery

First verify parser/source health and distinct report IDs. Then inspect process/bundle/version/signature, OS/build/architecture, exception type/signal/codes, termination reason, crashing thread and symbols through authorized tools, recent application/OS/config rollout, CPU/memory/disk pressure, plug-ins, hardware diagnostics, and user impact. Apple crash fields guide diagnosis but do not establish maliciousness.

Do not automatically kill/relaunch applications, delete reports/preferences/caches, upload reports externally, collect full user data, roll back software, or reboot from Splunk. Use application and endpoint change control. Close after the responsible build/config/hardware action and a monitored no-recurrence window, preserving original protected evidence. Missing crashes with user complaints indicate collection or a different hang/termination path; route to source health, hang/spindump, Unified Log, or application telemetry rather than declaring recovery.
grandmaExplanation: We count distinct fatal crash reports for the same app on the same Mac. Three in fifteen minutes gets attention, while private report details stay restricted to the people fixing the app.
